title: Protocol Canary fixture (schema_version 1)
description: A single compatibility-assertion fixture consumed by StellarCanary/Protocol-Canary's canary-fixtures loader. This schema mirrors that implementation (see Protocol-Canary's docs/fixture-contract.md); it is a convenience for editor/CI linting in this repository, not an independent specification. On any disagreement, Protocol-Canary's implementation is authoritative. Note: this top-level object intentionally leaves additionalProperties unset, so unknown top-level fields are permitted (not rejected) — matching tools/validate/validate.py, which performs no unknown-field check. tools/validate/schema_sync.py checks this schema's enums and required-field lists against tools/validate/validate.py's constants, so the two cannot drift unnoticed. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the rationale.
$comment: examples mirrors protocol-28/xdr/cap-0085/p28-xdr-cap85-external-ref-roundtrip.toml; keep the two in sync.

examples.description: ContractExecutable using the CAP-0085 CONTRACT_EXECUTABLE_EXTERNAL_REF case round-trips byte-for-byte

id.description: Unique across every fixture loaded from a given --fixtures-dir, not just within this file. Convention (not enforced by the loader): p<protocol>-<surface>-<slug>.

protocol.description: The Stellar protocol version this fixture targets. A run whose --protocol does not match is skipped, not failed.

surface.description: Selects which surface crate parses the fixture body. Any other value fails to parse.

category.description: Free-text grouping, e.g. a CAP slug ("cap-0083") or "network"/"smoke". tools/validate/validate.py rejects the vague values "misc", "other", "test" and "general" as errors, in any letter case; use a specific CAP or topic slug instead.

source_reference.description: An authoritative upstream reference: a CAP identifier such as CAP-0083, or an absolute https:// URL to a CAP, an upstream XDR definition, or an official release/API doc. Required for every protocol-specific fixture in this repository: tools/validate/validate.py reports a missing or empty source_reference as an error, so omitting it fails validation and CI.
source_reference.$comment: The pattern is the syntactic rule and is kept identical to SOURCE_REFERENCE_PATTERN in tools/validate/validate.py (tools/validate/schema_sync.py checks it). That a github.com or raw.githubusercontent.com link is pinned to a commit or tag, not a branch, cannot be expressed here and is enforced only by validate.py, like the other loader-side invariants.

required_capabilities.description: kebab-case canary_core::Capability values. A fixture requiring a capability the target project lacks is skipped, not failed. This enum must be kept in sync with CAPABILITIES in tools/validate/validate.py and with canary_core::Capability in StellarCanary/Protocol-Canary; the two lists are maintained independently (a JSON Schema enum and a Python set), so a new capability added to one without the other silently creates a validator/schema mismatch.

input_file.description: Path to an externally stored input file, relative to this fixture file's own directory. Existence is checked by the validator; the loader does not read the file's contents itself. This is the external-file alternative to inlining the input via value_base64 - a fixture supplies its input one way or the other, not both. Prefer an external file for large inputs (e.g. a multi-kilobyte binary payload) and value_base64 for short XDR values. (Note: Currently unused by any existing fixture in this repository; XDR inputs are inlined via value_base64.)

expected_file.description: Path to an externally stored expected-output file, relative to this fixture file's own directory. Existence is checked by the validator; like input_file, the loader does not read the file's contents itself. This is the external-file alternative to inlining the expected value via expected_base64 (used with kind = encode-equals) - a fixture supplies the expected value one way or the other, not both. Prefer an external file for large expected payloads and expected_base64 for short XDR values. (Note: Currently unused by any existing fixture in this repository; expected values are inlined via expected_base64.)

type.description: The XDR type name canary-xdr should decode value_base64 as.

value.description: Required when kind = field-equals; compared for exact equality against the decoded JSON value of 'field' in the method's response. Its type is intentionally unconstrained (any JSON/TOML value is accepted) but in practice it must match the JSON type the targeted RPC field actually returns — e.g. protocolVersion is a number and passphrase is a string. An array or inline table only ever matches a field that itself returns an array or object. The JSON type names a field-type assertion may use are listed on expected_type below; there is no equivalent fixed list for value because it is compared to real response data, not to a type name.

expected_type.description: JSON type names accepted for an RPC field-type assertion. Keep this enum in sync with RPC_ASSERT_TYPES in tools/validate/validate.py.

message_contains.description: Optional, and only meaningful with kind = simulation-error: a substring the simulation's error message must contain. Omit it to assert only that the simulation failed. It must be a non-empty string when present -- canary-soroban reads it as Option<String> via as_str, so a non-string is silently dropped and an empty string matches every message, either way weakening the assertion without any visible error.

expect.$comment: additionalProperties mirrors canary-soroban's unknown_body_keys(expect, ["kind", "message_contains"]), which rejects any other key. Unlike the top level of a fixture, where unknown fields are deliberately permitted, [expect] is closed upstream.
